## Approach

For this assignment, I will use the same chess tournament data from Project 1. Instead of calculating the average rating of each player's opponents, I will use the player's pre-rating and each opponent's pre-rating to calculate an expected score for every game.

I will use the Elo expected-score formula shown in the course reference video:

`1 / (1 + 10^((opponent rating - player rating) / 400))`

After calculating the expected score for each matchup, I will add the values for each player to get the player's expected tournament score. I will then subtract the expected score from the actual tournament points.

A positive difference means the player scored more points than expected. A negative difference means the player scored fewer points than expected. I will sort the results and report the five players who overperformed the most and the five who underperformed the most.

I will also check Gary Hua's calculation separately so I can compare the manual result with the result produced by the code.
